Natural_Language: This part prescribes policies, procedures, and contract format for the acquisition of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_100_a: Part 41 prescribes policies for acquisition of utility services; P_41_100_b: Part 41 prescribes procedures for acquisition of utility services; P_41_100_c: Part 41 prescribes contract format for acquisition of utility services
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement. Three functions (policies, procedures, contract format) are all prescribed by this part. Conjunction accurately captures that all three are within scope.

Natural_Language: Definitions used in Part 41 for acquisition of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101: Definitions for Part 41 consist of defined terms in 41.101(a) through 41.101(k)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for all definitions. All defined terms collectively constitute the definitional framework for Part 41.

Natural_Language: Areawide contract means a contract entered into between the General Services Administration (GSA) and a utility service supplier to cover utility service needs of Federal agencies within the franchise territory of the supplier. Each areawide contract includes an "Authorization" form for requesting service, connection, disconnection, or change in service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_a_1: Areawide contract is a contract between GSA and a utility service supplier; P_41_101_a_2: Areawide contract covers utility service needs of Federal agencies within supplier franchise territory; P_41_101_a_3: Each areawide contract includes an Authorization form for requesting service, connection, disconnection, or change in service
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition with three conjunctive elements: parties, scope, and included form. All elements are constitutive of the definition.

Natural_Language: Authorization means the document executed by the ordering agency and the utility supplier to order service under an areawide contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_b: Authorization is a document executed by ordering agency and utility supplier to order service under an areawide contract
Validation_Notes: Simple definitional proposition. Already atomic. Authorization is defined by its parties, purpose, and governing vehicle.

Natural_Language: Connection charge means all nonrecurring costs, whether refundable or nonrefundable, to be paid by the Government to the utility supplier for the required connecting facilities, which are installed, owned, operated, and maintained by the utility supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_c_1: Connection charge is all nonrecurring costs paid by Government to utility supplier; P_41_101_c_2: Connection charge covers refundable or nonrefundable costs; P_41_101_c_3: Costs are for required connecting facilities installed, owned, operated, and maintained by utility supplier
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition. Three elements define the scope: cost type (nonrecurring), refundability (both), and facility ownership (supplier). Cross-reference to Termination liability noted in source text.

Natural_Language: Federal Power and Water Marketing Agency means a Government entity that produces, manages, transports, controls, and sells electrical and water supply service to customers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_d: Federal Power and Water Marketing Agency is a Government entity that produces, manages, transports, controls, and sells electrical and water supply service to customers
Validation_Notes: Simple definitional proposition. The five functions (produces, manages, transports, controls, sells) collectively define the entity type. Treated as atomic because the functions are inseparable in defining the term.

Natural_Language: Franchise territory means a geographical area that a utility supplier has a right to serve based upon a franchise, a certificate of public convenience and necessity, or other legal means.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_e_1: Franchise territory is a geographical area a utility supplier has right to serve; P_41_101_e_2: Right to serve is based upon a franchise, certificate of public convenience and necessity, or other legal means
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition with two elements: geographic scope and legal basis. The legal basis options (franchise, certificate, other legal means) are disjunctive within the second atomic but treated as a single atomic because they collectively describe the basis.

Natural_Language: Intervention means action by GSA or a delegated agency to formally participate in a utility regulatory proceeding on behalf of all Federal executive agencies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_f: Intervention is action by GSA or delegated agency to formally participate in a utility regulatory proceeding on behalf of all Federal executive agencies
Validation_Notes: Simple definitional proposition. Actor (GSA or delegated agency), action (formal participation), venue (utility regulatory proceeding), and beneficiary (all Federal executive agencies) are inseparable components.

Natural_Language: Rates may include rate schedules, riders, rules, terms and conditions of service, and other tariff and service charges, e.g., facilities use charges.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_g: Rates may include rate schedules, riders, rules, terms and conditions of service, and other tariff and service charges
Validation_Notes: Permissive definition using "may include" indicates non-exhaustive list. Treated as atomic since the enumerated items collectively define the permissive scope. Flagged PENDING_REVIEW due to advisory/permissive language.

Natural_Language: Separate contract means a utility services contract (other than a GSA areawide contract, an Authorization under an areawide contract, or an interagency agreement) to cover the acquisition of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_h_1: Separate contract is a utility services contract for acquisition of utility services; P_41_101_h_2: Separate contract excludes GSA areawide contracts, Authorizations under areawide contracts, and interagency agreements
Validation_Notes: Definitional proposition defined both by what it is (utility services contract) and what it excludes (three other contract types). Negation applied to the exclusion clause.

Natural_Language: Termination liability means a contingent Government obligation to pay a utility supplier the unamortized portion of a connection charge and any other applicable nonrefundable service charge as defined in the contract in the event the Government terminates the contract before the cost of connection facilities has been recovered by the utility supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_i_1: Termination liability is a contingent Government obligation; P_41_101_i_2: Obligation is to pay utility supplier unamortized portion of connection charge and applicable nonrefundable service charges; P_41_101_i_3: Obligation arises when Government terminates contract before cost recovery by utility supplier
Validation_Notes: Conditional definition: the obligation (conjunction of contingency and payment) is triggered by the condition of early termination. Material implication used because the liability only exists upon the triggering event. HIGH-RISK flag due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Utility service includes, but is not limited to, a continuous service such as furnishing electricity, natural or manufactured gas, water, sewerage, thermal energy, chilled water, steam, hot water, or high temperature hot water for use in the United States.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_j: Utility service includes continuous services such as electricity, natural or manufactured gas, water, sewerage, thermal energy, chilled water, steam, hot water, or high temperature hot water for use in the United States
Validation_Notes: Inclusive definitional proposition. "Includes but is not limited to" makes this non-exhaustive. The enumerated services are examples within the broader definition. Treated as atomic because the list collectively defines the inclusion scope.

Natural_Language: Utility services does not include: any of the above when purchased for use in a foreign country, broadband internet, non-broadcast television, telecommunications services, information technology services, acquisitions of natural or manufactured gas when not purchased as utility services (i.e., when purchased as commodities), or acquisitions of rights in real property, acquisitions of public utility facilities, and on-site equipment needed for the facility's own distribution system, or construction/maintenance of Government-owned equipment and real property.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_101_k: Utility service excludes foreign-use purchases, broadband internet, non-broadcast television, telecommunications services, IT services, gas purchased as commodities, real property rights, public utility facility acquisitions, on-site distribution equipment, and Government-owned equipment construction/maintenance
Validation_Notes: Exclusionary definitional proposition. Negation applied to represent items outside the definition of utility service. All exclusions are mandatory and conjunctive (all are excluded). Treated as atomic since all items share the same logical status of exclusion.

Natural_Language: Applicability of Part 41.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102: Applicability provisions consist of general applicability and exceptions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Applicability defined by both the general rule and the exceptions.

Natural_Language: Except as provided in paragraph (b) of this section, this part applies to the acquisition of utility services for the Government, including connection charges and termination liabilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102_a_1: Part 41 applies to acquisition of utility services for the Government; P_41_102_a_2: Applicability includes connection charges; P_41_102_a_3: Applicability includes termination liabilities; P_41_102_a_4: Applicability is subject to exceptions in 41.102(b)
Validation_Notes: Conditional applicability: Part 41 applies unless exceptions in (b) are triggered. Material implication with negated antecedent represents "except as provided" structure. HIGH-RISK flag due to Rule 15.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to the exceptions listed in 41.102(b)(1) through (b)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102_b: Exceptions to Part 41 applicability
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for exceptions. Disjunction used because any single exception independently removes applicability.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to utility services produced, distributed, or sold by another Federal agency. In those cases, agencies must use interagency agreements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102_b_1_a: Part 41 does not apply to utility services produced, distributed, or sold by another Federal agency; P_41_102_b_1_b: When utility services are from another Federal agency, agencies must use interagency agreements
Validation_Notes: Two-part proposition: exclusion from Part 41 and mandatory alternative (interagency agreements). The exclusion triggers the interagency agreement requirement. HIGH-RISK flag for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to utility services obtained by purchase, exchange, or otherwise by a Federal power or water marketing agency incident to that agency's marketing or distribution program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102_b_2: Part 41 does not apply to utility services obtained by Federal power or water marketing agency incident to its marketing or distribution program
Validation_Notes: Exclusionary proposition. Federal power/water marketing agencies operating within their marketing/distribution programs are exempt from Part 41.

Natural_Language: This part does not apply to third party financed shared-savings projects authorized by 42 U.S.C. 8287. However, agencies may utilize part 41 for any energy savings or purchased utility service directly resulting from implementation of a third party financed shared-savings project under 42 U.S.C. 8287 for periods not to exceed 25 years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_102_b_3_a: Part 41 does not apply to third party financed shared-savings projects under 42 U.S.C. 8287; P_41_102_b_3_b: Agencies may utilize Part 41 for energy savings or purchased utility service from shared-savings projects for periods not exceeding 25 years
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Two-part proposition: general exclusion plus permissive authority to use Part 41 for resulting services. "May utilize" creates discretionary authority represented by tautology. The 25-year period limit is embedded in the permissive clause. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Statutory and delegated authority for acquisition of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103: Statutory and delegated authority provisions for Part 41
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition encompassing statutory authority, delegated authority, and certification requirements.

Natural_Language: Statutory authority for utility services acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_a: Statutory authority provisions for GSA, DOD, and DOE
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for statutory authorities of three agencies.

Natural_Language: The General Services Administration (GSA) is authorized by 40 U.S.C. 501 to prescribe policies and methods governing the acquisition and supply of utility services for Federal agencies. This authority includes related functions such as managing public utility services and representing Federal agencies in proceedings before Federal and state regulatory bodies. GSA is authorized by 40 U.S.C. 501 to contract for utility services for periods not exceeding ten years.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_a_1_a: GSA is authorized by 40 U.S.C. 501 to prescribe policies and methods for utility services acquisition; P_41_103_a_1_b: GSA authority includes managing public utility services and representing Federal agencies in regulatory proceedings; P_41_103_a_1_c: GSA is authorized to contract for utility services for periods not exceeding ten years
Validation_Notes: Declarative statutory authority. Three conjunctive elements: policy authority, scope of functions, and contract period limit. All derive from 40 U.S.C. 501.

Natural_Language: The Department of Defense (DOD) is authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3201(a), and 40 U.S.C. 113(e)(3) to acquire utility services for military facilities.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_a_2: DOD is authorized by 10 U.S.C. 3201(a) and 40 U.S.C. 113(e)(3) to acquire utility services for military facilities
Validation_Notes: Simple statutory authority declaration. DOD authority is scoped to military facilities.

Natural_Language: The Department of Energy (DOE) is authorized by the Department of Energy Organization Act (42 U.S.C. 7251, et seq.) to acquire utility services. DOE is authorized by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2204), to enter into new contracts or modify existing contracts for electric services for periods not exceeding 25 years for uranium enrichment installations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_a_3_a: DOE is authorized by 42 U.S.C. 7251 et seq. to acquire utility services; P_41_103_a_3_b: DOE is authorized by 42 U.S.C. 2204 to contract for electric services for uranium enrichment installations for periods not exceeding 25 years
Validation_Notes: Two separate statutory authorities for DOE: general utility services and specific electric services for uranium enrichment with 25-year period limit.

Natural_Language: GSA has delegated its authority to enter into utility service contracts for periods not exceeding ten years to DOD and DOE, and for connection charges only, to the Department of Veteran Affairs. Contracting pursuant to this delegated authority must be consistent with the requirements of this part. Other agencies requiring utility service contracts for periods over one year, but not exceeding ten years, may request a delegation of authority from GSA at utilities@gsa.gov. In keeping with its statutory authority, GSA will, as necessary, conduct reviews of delegated agencies' acquisitions of utility services to ensure compliance with the terms of the delegation and applicable laws and regulations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_b_a: GSA delegated utility contract authority (up to 10 years) to DOD and DOE; P_41_103_b_b: GSA delegated connection charge authority only to VA; P_41_103_b_c: Delegated contracting must be consistent with Part 41 requirements; P_41_103_b_d: Other agencies may request delegation from GSA for contracts over 1 year but not exceeding 10 years; P_41_103_b_e: GSA will conduct reviews of delegated agencies for compliance
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-element provision. Delegation to DOD/DOE/VA is mandatory factual. Consistency requirement is mandatory. "May request" creates permissive authority (tautology). GSA review authority is declarative. Flagged for review due to mixed mandatory/permissive elements.

Natural_Language: Requests for delegations of contracting authority from GSA must include a certification from the acquiring agency's Senior Procurement Executive that the agency has met the requirements in 41.103(c)(1) through (c)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_c: Delegation requests must include SPE certification of requirements in (c)(1) through (c)(3)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three certification elements are mandatory conjunctive requirements for delegation requests.

Natural_Language: An established acquisition program.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_c_1: Agency has an established acquisition program
Validation_Notes: Simple certification requirement. Agency must demonstrate an existing acquisition program.

Natural_Language: Personnel technically qualified to deal with specialized utilities problems.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_c_2: Agency has personnel technically qualified for specialized utilities problems
Validation_Notes: Simple certification requirement. Agency must have qualified personnel.

Natural_Language: The ability to accomplish its own pre-award contract review.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_103_c_3: Agency has ability to accomplish its own pre-award contract review
Validation_Notes: Simple certification requirement. Agency must have internal pre-award review capability.

Natural_Language: Policy for acquisition of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201: Policy provisions for utility services acquisition
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for policy section. Note: source text skips paragraph (c), going from (b) to (d).

Natural_Language: Subject to paragraph (d) of this section, it is the policy of the Federal Government that agencies obtain required utility services from sources of supply which are most advantageous to the Government in terms of economy, efficiency, reliability, or service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_a_1: Federal policy requires agencies to obtain utility services from most advantageous sources; P_41_201_a_2: Advantage is measured in terms of economy, efficiency, reliability, or service; P_41_201_a_3: Policy is subject to restrictions in 41.201(d)
Validation_Notes: Policy statement with conditional applicability. "Subject to paragraph (d)" creates dependency. The four evaluation criteria (economy, efficiency, reliability, service) are disjunctive within the second atomic -- any one can establish advantage. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Except for acquisitions at or below the simplified acquisition threshold, agencies must acquire utility services by a bilateral written contract, which must include the clauses required by 41.501, regardless of whether rates or terms and conditions of service are fixed or adjusted by a regulatory body. Agencies may not use the utility supplier's forms and clauses to avoid the inclusion of provisions and clauses required by 41.501 or by statute.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_b_a: For acquisitions above SAT, agencies must acquire utility services by bilateral written contract; P_41_201_b_b: Bilateral written contract must include clauses required by 41.501; P_41_201_b_c: Contract clause requirement applies regardless of whether rates are fixed or adjusted by regulatory body; P_41_201_b_d: Agencies may not use supplier forms to avoid required provisions and clauses
Validation_Notes: Multi-element mandatory requirement. SAT exception creates implicit conditional for the bilateral contract requirement. Prohibition on using supplier forms to circumvent requirements is a separate mandatory negation. All elements are conjunctive mandates.

Natural_Language: Restrictions and exceptions related to DOD Appropriations Act Section 8093 on electricity purchases.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d: DOD Appropriations Act restrictions consist of the general restriction and its exceptions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for DOD Appropriations Act restrictions on electricity purchases. Contains the restriction, its exceptions, and additional authorities.

Natural_Language: Section 8093 of the Department of Defense Appropriations Act of 1988, Pub. L. 100-202, provides that none of the funds appropriated by that Act or any other Act with respect to any fiscal year by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States, may be used for the purchase of electricity by the Government in any manner that is inconsistent with state law governing the providing of electric utility service, including state utility commission rulings and electric utility franchises or service territories established pursuant to state statute, state regulation, or state-approved territorial agreements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_1_a: No Federal funds may be used for electricity purchases inconsistent with state law; P_41_201_d_1_b: State law includes state utility commission rulings and electric utility franchises or service territories
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on inconsistent electricity purchases. Negation captures the "may not" restriction. Second atomic defines scope of state law for purposes of the prohibition.

Natural_Language: The Act does not preclude the exceptions listed in 41.201(d)(2)(i) through (iii).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_2: Exceptions to Section 8093 restriction
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for exceptions. Disjunction because any single exception independently applies.

Natural_Language: The head of a Federal agency from entering into a contract pursuant to 42 U.S.C. 8287 (which pertains to the subject of shared energy savings including cogeneration).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_2_i: Section 8093 does not preclude agency head contracts under 42 U.S.C. 8287 for shared energy savings
Validation_Notes: Exception to electricity purchase restriction. Shared energy savings contracts are preserved.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of a military department from entering into a contract pursuant to 10 U.S.C. 2922a (which pertains to contracts for energy or fuel for military installations including the provision and operation of energy production facilities).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_2_ii: Section 8093 does not preclude military department Secretary contracts under 10 U.S.C. 2922a for military installation energy/fuel
Validation_Notes: Exception to electricity purchase restriction. Military energy/fuel contracts are preserved.

Natural_Language: The Secretary of a military department from purchasing electricity from any provider when the utility or utilities having applicable state-approved franchise or other service authorizations are found by the Secretary to be unwilling or unable to meet unusual standards for service reliability that are necessary for purposes of national defense.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_2_iii_a: Franchised utility is found unwilling or unable to meet unusual service reliability standards for national defense; P_41_201_d_2_iii_b: Secretary of military department may purchase electricity from any provider
Validation_Notes: Conditional permissive authority. The Secretary finding of inability/unwillingness triggers discretionary purchasing authority. "May" creates tautology. National defense necessity is the qualifying condition. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Additionally, the head of a Federal agency may exercise authorities in 41.201(d)(3)(i) through (iii).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_3: Additional agency head authorities
Validation_Notes: Parent for additional permissive authorities. Disjunction because each authority is independently exercisable.

Natural_Language: Consistent with applicable state law, enter into contracts for the purchase or transfer of electricity to the agency by a non-utility, including a qualifying facility under the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_3_i_a: Contracts must be consistent with applicable state law; P_41_201_d_3_i_b: Agency head may enter contracts for purchase or transfer of electricity by non-utility
Validation_Notes: Conditional permissive authority. State law consistency is required condition. "May" creates discretion. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Enter into an interagency agreement, pursuant to 41.206 and 17.5, with a Federal power marketing agency or the Tennessee Valley Authority for the transfer of electric power to the agency.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_3_ii: Agency head may enter interagency agreement with Federal power marketing agency or TVA for electric power transfer pursuant to 41.206 and 17.5
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority. "May" creates discretionary power. Reference to 41.206 and 17.5 establishes procedural dependency.

Natural_Language: Enter into a contract with an electric utility under the authority or tariffs of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_d_3_iii: Agency head may enter contract with electric utility under FERC authority or tariffs
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority under FERC framework. "May" creates discretion.

Natural_Language: Prior to acquiring electric utility services on a competitive basis, the contracting officer must determine, with the advice of legal counsel, by a market survey or any other appropriate means, e.g. consultation with the state agency responsible for regulating public utilities, that such competition would not be inconsistent with state law governing the provision of electric utility service, including state utility commission rulings and electric utility franchises or service territories established pursuant to state statute, state regulation, or state-approved territorial agreements. Proposals from alternative electric suppliers must provide a representation that service can be provided in a manner consistent with section 8093 of Public Law 100-202.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_201_e_a: Prior to competitive electric acquisition, CO must determine competition is not inconsistent with state law; P_41_201_e_b: Determination must be made with advice of legal counsel; P_41_201_e_c: Determination may be by market survey or other appropriate means; P_41_201_e_d: Proposals from alternative suppliers must include representation of consistency with Section 8093
Validation_Notes: Multi-element mandatory pre-acquisition requirement. All four elements must be satisfied before competitive electric acquisition proceeds. State law consistency determination is the core requirement.

Natural_Language: Procedures for acquiring utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202: Procedural requirements for utility service acquisition
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for procedures section.

Natural_Language: Agencies must conduct market surveys and perform acquisition planning in order to promote and provide for full and open competition provided that the contracting officer determines that any resultant contract would not be inconsistent with applicable state law governing the provision of electric utility services. If competition for an entire utility service is not available, the market survey may be used to determine the availability of competitive sources for certain portions of the requirement. The scope of the term "entire utility service" includes the provision of the utility service capacity, energy, water, sewage, transportation, standby or back-up service, transmission and/or distribution service, quality assurance, system reliability, system operation and maintenance, metering, and billing.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_a_1: Agencies must conduct market surveys and acquisition planning for full and open competition; P_41_202_a_2: Competition must not be inconsistent with applicable state law for electric utility services; P_41_202_a_3: If full competition unavailable, market survey may assess competitive sources for portions of requirement; P_41_202_a_4: "Entire utility service" includes capacity, energy, water, sewage, transportation, standby, transmission/distribution, quality assurance, reliability, operations/maintenance, metering, and billing
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Complex provision with conditional and permissive elements. Market survey is mandatory when state law permits competition. Partial competition is permissive when full competition is unavailable. Definition of "entire utility service" is declarative. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: In performing a market survey, the contracting officer must consider the alternatives in 41.202(b)(1) through (b)(3).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_b: Market survey must consider listed alternatives
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. All three alternatives must be considered (conjunctive requirement).

Natural_Language: GSA areawide contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_b_1: CO must consider GSA areawide contracts in market survey
Validation_Notes: Simple mandatory consideration element.

Natural_Language: Separate contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_b_2: CO must consider separate contracts in market survey
Validation_Notes: Simple mandatory consideration element.

Natural_Language: Interagency agreements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_b_3: CO must consider interagency agreements in market survey
Validation_Notes: Simple mandatory consideration element.

Natural_Language: When a utility supplier refuses to execute a tendered contract, the agency must obtain a written definite and final refusal signed by a corporate officer or other responsible official of the supplier (or if unobtainable, document any unwritten refusal), and transmit this document, along with statements of the reasons for the refusal and the record of negotiations, to GSA at utilities@gsa.gov. Unless urgent and compelling circumstances exist, the contracting officer must notify GSA prior to acquiring utility services without executing a tendered contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_c_a: Upon supplier refusal, agency must obtain written definite and final refusal from corporate officer; P_41_202_c_b: If written refusal unobtainable, agency must document unwritten refusal; P_41_202_c_c: Agency must transmit refusal document with reasons and negotiation record to GSA; P_41_202_c_d: Unless urgent and compelling circumstances, CO must notify GSA before acquiring without executed contract
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Addition (Add): Rule 8; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Complex procedural requirement triggered by supplier refusal. Written or documented unwritten refusal (disjunctive). GSA transmission is mandatory. GSA notification has an exception for urgent circumstances. Parent for acquisition methods in (c)(1) and (c)(2). HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: By issuing a purchase order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_c_1: Agency may acquire utility services by issuing a purchase order after supplier refusal
Validation_Notes: Alternative acquisition method after supplier refusal. Purchase order pathway.

Natural_Language: By ordering the necessary utility service and paying for it upon the presentation of an invoice, provided that a determination is approved by the head of the contracting activity that a written contract cannot be obtained and that the issuance of a purchase order is not feasible.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_c_2_a: Agency may order utility service and pay upon invoice presentation; P_41_202_c_2_b: HCA must approve determination that written contract cannot be obtained; P_41_202_c_2_c: HCA must approve determination that purchase order issuance is not feasible
Validation_Notes: Conditional acquisition method. Both HCA determinations (no written contract possible AND no purchase order feasible) must be met before invoice-based ordering is authorized. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: When obtaining service without a bilateral written contract, the contracting officer must establish a utility history file on each acquisition of utility service provided by a contractor.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d: When obtaining service without bilateral contract, CO must establish utility history file containing items in (d)(1) through (d)(6)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for utility history file requirements. All six elements are mandatory file contents. Triggered by absence of bilateral written contract.

Natural_Language: The unsigned, tendered contract and any related letter of transmittal.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_1: Utility history file must contain unsigned tendered contract and related transmittal letter
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element.

Natural_Language: The reasons stated by the utility supplier for not executing the tendered contract, the record of negotiations, and a written definite and final refusal by a corporate officer or other responsible official of the supplier (or if unobtainable, documentation of unwritten refusal).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_2: Utility history file must contain supplier reasons for non-execution, negotiation record, and written/documented refusal
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element. Mirrors documentation requirement from 41.202(c).

Natural_Language: Services to be furnished and the estimated annual cost.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_3: Utility history file must contain description of services and estimated annual cost
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element.

Natural_Language: Historical record of any applicable connection charges.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_4: Utility history file must contain historical record of applicable connection charges
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element.

Natural_Language: Historical record of any applicable ongoing capital credits.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_5: Utility history file must contain historical record of applicable capital credits
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element.

Natural_Language: A copy of the applicable rate schedule.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_d_6: Utility history file must contain copy of applicable rate schedule
Validation_Notes: Mandatory file content element.

Natural_Language: If the Government obtains utility service pursuant to paragraph (c) of this section, on an annual basis beginning from the date of final refusal, take action to execute a bilateral written contract. The contracting officer must document the utility history file with the efforts made and the agency must notify GSA, in writing at utilities@gsa.gov, if the utility continues to refuse to execute a bilateral contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_202_e_a: If Government obtains service under 41.202(c), agency must annually attempt to execute bilateral written contract; P_41_202_e_b: CO must document utility history file with efforts made; P_41_202_e_c: Agency must notify GSA in writing if utility continues to refuse bilateral contract
Validation_Notes: Conditional annual obligation triggered by service obtained without bilateral contract. Three conjunctive requirements: annual bilateral attempt, documentation, and GSA notification. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_203: GSA assistance provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for GSA assistance.

Natural_Language: GSA will, upon request, provide technical and acquisition assistance, or will delegate its contracting authority for the furnishing of the services described in this part for any Federal agency, mixed-ownership Government corporation, the District of Columbia, the Senate, the House of Representatives, or the Architect of the Capitol and any activity under the Architect's direction.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_203_a_1: GSA will provide technical and acquisition assistance upon request; P_41_203_a_2: GSA will delegate contracting authority upon request; P_41_203_a_3: Assistance/delegation available to Federal agencies, mixed-ownership Government corporations, DC, Senate, House, and Architect of the Capitol
Validation_Notes: GSA offers either assistance or delegation (disjunctive) to a defined set of eligible entities. "Will" is declarative, establishing GSA obligation upon request.

Natural_Language: Agencies, seeking assistance must provide upon request by GSA the information listed in 41.301.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_203_b: Agencies seeking GSA assistance must provide information listed in 41.301 upon GSA request
Validation_Notes: Mandatory information requirement triggered by GSA request. Cross-reference to 41.301.

Natural_Language: GSA areawide contracts provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204: GSA areawide contract provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for areawide contracts. Covers purpose, features, procedures, and notification.

Natural_Language: GSA enters into areawide contracts for use by Federal agencies. Areawide contracts provide a pre-established contractual vehicle for ordering utility services under the conditions in paragraph (c)(1) of this section.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_a_1: GSA enters areawide contracts for use by Federal agencies; P_41_204_a_2: Areawide contracts provide pre-established vehicle for ordering utility services
Validation_Notes: Declarative purpose statement. Two conjunctive elements define the purpose of areawide contracts.

Natural_Language: Features of areawide contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_b: Features of areawide contracts
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for areawide contract features.

Natural_Language: Areawide contracts generally provide for ordering utility service at rates approved and/or established by a regulatory body and published in a tariff or rate schedule. However, agencies are permitted to negotiate other rates and terms and conditions of service with the supplier. Rates other than those published may require the approval of the regulatory body.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_b_1_a: Areawide contracts generally provide ordering at regulatory-approved rates published in tariff or rate schedule; P_41_204_b_1_b: Agencies are permitted to negotiate other rates and terms with supplier; P_41_204_b_1_c: Non-published rates may require regulatory body approval
Validation_Notes: Mixed mandatory/permissive provision. General rate framework is declarative. Agency negotiation authority is permissive (tautology). Regulatory approval for non-published rates is advisory ("may require"). Flagged for mixed modal verbs.

Natural_Language: Areawide contracts are negotiated with utility service suppliers for the provision of service within the supplier's franchise territory or service area.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_b_2: Areawide contracts are negotiated with suppliers for service within franchise territory or service area
Validation_Notes: Declarative feature statement. Geographic scope is limited to franchise territory or service area.

Natural_Language: Due to the regulated nature of the utility industry, as well as statutory restrictions associated with the procurement of electricity, competition is typically not available within the entire geographical area covered by an areawide contract, although it may be available at specific locations within the utility's service area. When competing suppliers are available, the provisions of paragraph (c)(1) of this section apply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_b_3_a: Competition is typically not available within entire areawide contract area; P_41_204_b_3_b: Competition may be available at specific locations; P_41_204_b_3_c: When competing suppliers are available, 41.204(c)(1) applies
Validation_Notes: Descriptive provision with conditional trigger. When competition exists at specific locations, competitive procedures apply. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Procedures for obtaining service under areawide contracts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c: Procedures for obtaining areawide contract service
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for areawide contract service procedures.

Natural_Language: Any Federal agency having a requirement for utility services within an area covered by an areawide contract must acquire services under that areawide contract unless exceptions in (c)(1)(i) or (c)(1)(ii) apply.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c_1: Federal agencies must use areawide contract for utility services in covered areas unless exceptions apply
Validation_Notes: Mandatory use requirement with two exceptions. Areawide contract is default vehicle. "Unless" creates conditional with negated exceptions as antecedent. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Service is available from more than one supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c_1_i_a: Service is available from more than one supplier; P_41_204_c_1_i_b: Service must be acquired using competitive acquisition procedures
Validation_Notes: Exception to mandatory areawide contract use. Multiple suppliers trigger competitive acquisition. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: The head of the contracting activity or designee otherwise determines that use of the areawide contract is not advantageous to the Government. The determination must be documented in the contract file with an information copy furnished to GSA at utilities@gsa.gov.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c_1_ii_a: HCA or designee determines areawide contract is not advantageous; P_41_204_c_1_ii_b: Determination must be documented in contract file; P_41_204_c_1_ii_c: Information copy must be furnished to GSA
Validation_Notes: Conditional exception. HCA determination triggers documentation and GSA notification requirements. Both post-determination actions are mandatory. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Each areawide contract includes an authorization form for ordering service, connection, disconnection, or change in service. Upon execution of an authorization by the contracting officer and utility supplier, the utility supplier is required to furnish services, without further negotiation, at the current, applicable published or unpublished rates, unless other rates, and/or terms and conditions are separately negotiated by the Federal agency with the supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c_2_a: Each areawide contract includes authorization form for service orders; P_41_204_c_2_b: Upon authorization execution, supplier must furnish services at current applicable rates without further negotiation; P_41_204_c_2_c: Other rates and terms may be separately negotiated
Validation_Notes: Authorization execution triggers supplier obligation. Default is current rates without negotiation. Separate negotiation is permissive (tautology). Mixed mandatory/permissive elements.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must execute the authorization, and attach it to a Standard Form (SF) 26, Award/Contract, along with any modifications such as connection charges, special facilities, or service arrangements. The contracting officer must also attach any specific fiscal, operational, and administrative requirements of the agency, applicable rate schedules, technical information and detailed maps or drawings of delivery points, details on Government ownership, maintenance, or repair of facilities, and other information deemed necessary to fully define the service conditions in the authorization/contract.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_c_3_a: CO must execute authorization and attach to SF 26; P_41_204_c_3_b: CO must attach modifications (connection charges, special facilities, service arrangements); P_41_204_c_3_c: CO must attach fiscal, operational, administrative requirements, rate schedules, technical info, maps, ownership details, and other necessary information
Validation_Notes: Multi-element mandatory procedural requirement. All attachments are required. CO must execute and attach all specified documentation.

Natural_Language: Agencies must provide a copy of each SF 26 and executed authorization issued under an areawide contract to GSA at utilities@gsa.gov within 30 days after execution.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_204_f_a: Agencies must provide copy of SF 26 and executed authorization to GSA; P_41_204_f_b: Copy must be provided within 30 days after execution
Validation_Notes: Mandatory notification with time limit. Both the action (provide copy) and timing (30 days) are mandatory.

Natural_Language: Separate contracts provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205: Separate contract provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for separate contracts.

Natural_Language: In the absence of an areawide contract or interagency agreement, agencies must acquire utility services by separate contract subject to this part, and subject to agency contracting authority.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_a_1: Absence of areawide contract or interagency agreement triggers separate contract requirement; P_41_205_a_2: Separate contract must be subject to Part 41; P_41_205_a_3: Separate contract must be subject to agency contracting authority
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement. Absence of two preferred vehicles triggers separate contract obligation. Both Part 41 compliance and agency authority are required. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: If an agency enters into a separate contract, the contracting officer must document the contract file with the information in 41.205(b)(1) through (b)(6).

Natural_Language: The number of available suppliers.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_b_1: Contract file must document number of available suppliers
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element.

Natural_Language: Any special equipment, service reliability, or facility requirements and related costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_b_2: Contract file must document special equipment, reliability, facility requirements and related costs
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element.

Natural_Language: The utility supplier's rates, connection charges, and termination liability.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_b_3: Contract file must document supplier rates, connection charges, and termination liability
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element.

Natural_Language: Total estimated contract value (including costs in paragraphs (b)(2) and (3) of this subsection).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_b_4: Contract file must document total estimated contract value including costs from (b)(2) and (b)(3)
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element. Cross-references (b)(2) and (b)(3) for cost inclusion.

Natural_Language: Any technical or special contract terms required.

Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_b_6: Contract file must document unusual service characteristics
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation element.

Natural_Language: If requesting GSA assistance with a separate contract, the requesting agency must furnish the technical and acquisition data specified in 41.205(b), 41.301, and such other data as GSA may deem necessary.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_c_a: Agency requesting GSA assistance must furnish data from 41.205(b); P_41_205_c_b: Agency must furnish data from 41.301; P_41_205_c_c: Agency must furnish other data GSA deems necessary
Validation_Notes: Mandatory data provision for GSA assistance requests. Three conjunctive data sources: 41.205(b), 41.301, and GSA-determined additional data.

Natural_Language: A contract exceeding a 1-year period, but not exceeding ten years (except pursuant to 41.103), may be justified, and is usually required, where any of the circumstances in (d)(1) through (d)(3) exist.

Validation_Notes: Parent proposition. Any one of three circumstances independently justifies multi-year contract (disjunctive).

Natural_Language: The Government will obtain lower rates, larger discounts, or more favorable terms and conditions of service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_d_1: Multi-year contract justified when Government obtains lower rates, larger discounts, or more favorable terms
Validation_Notes: Justification circumstance. Any of the listed benefits (lower rates, larger discounts, better terms) satisfies this criterion.

Natural_Language: A proposed connection charge, termination liability, or any other facilities charge to be paid by the Federal Government will be reduced or eliminated.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_d_2: Multi-year contract justified when connection charges, termination liability, or facilities charges are reduced or eliminated
Validation_Notes: Justification circumstance. Charge reduction or elimination justifies multi-year approach.

Natural_Language: The utility service supplier refuses to render the desired service except under a contract exceeding a 1-year period.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_205_d_3: Multi-year contract justified when supplier refuses service except under multi-year contract
Validation_Notes: Justification circumstance. Supplier refusal to provide service on shorter terms justifies multi-year.

Natural_Language: Agencies must use interagency agreements (e.g., consolidated purchase, joint use, or cross-service agreements) when acquiring utility service or facilities from other Government agencies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_206_a: Agencies must use interagency agreements when acquiring utility service from other Government agencies; P_41_206_b: Interagency agreements include consolidated purchase, joint use, or cross-service agreements
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement for interagency agreements. "Must use" establishes mandatory vehicle when acquiring from other Government agencies. Examples provided are non-exhaustive.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_a: All requests for GSA delegations, assistance, and required submissions must be sent to GSA at utilities@gsa.gov

Natural_Language: Requests for contracting assistance for utility services must be sent not later than 120 days prior to the date new services are required to commence or an existing contract will expire. Requests must contain the information in (b)(1) through (b)(5).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_b_a: Requests must be sent no later than 120 days before new service commencement or contract expiration; P_41_301_b_b: Requests must contain information in (b)(1) through (b)(5)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition with timing requirement and content requirements. 120-day lead time is mandatory. All five content elements are required.

Natural_Language: A technical description or specification of the type, quantity, and quality of service required, and a delivery schedule.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_b_2: Request must contain copy of service proposal or proposed contract
Validation_Notes: Mandatory content element.

Natural_Language: Copies of all current published or unpublished rates of the utility supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_b_3: Request must contain copies of all current published or unpublished supplier rates
Validation_Notes: Mandatory content element. Covers both published and unpublished rates.

Natural_Language: Identification of any unusual factors affecting the acquisition.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_b_4: Request must identify unusual factors affecting acquisition
Validation_Notes: Mandatory content element.

Natural_Language: Identification of all available sources or methods of supply, an analysis of the cost effectiveness of each, and a statement of the ability of each source to provide the required services, including the location and a description of each available supplier's facilities at the nearest point of service, and the cost of providing or obtaining necessary backup and other ancillary services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_b_5_a: Request must identify all available sources or methods of supply; P_41_301_b_5_b: Request must include cost effectiveness analysis of each source; P_41_301_b_5_c: Request must include statement of each source's ability to provide services including facility details and backup service costs
Validation_Notes: Multi-element mandatory content requirement. Source identification, cost analysis, and capability statement are all required.

Natural_Language: For new utility service requirements, the agency must furnish the information in paragraph (a) of this section and the additional items in (c)(1) through (c)(7) as applicable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c: New service requirements must include (a) information plus items (c)(1) through (c)(7)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for new service requirements. All items are mandatory as applicable. Cross-references paragraph (a).

Natural_Language: The date initial service is required.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_1: Agency must furnish date initial service is required
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element.

Natural_Language: For the first 12 months of full service, estimated maximum demand, monthly consumption, other pertinent information (e.g., demand side management, load or energy management, peak shaving, on site generation, load shaping), and annual cost of the service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_2: Agency must furnish first 12-month estimates of maximum demand, monthly consumption, pertinent information, and annual cost
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element. Multiple data points for first year projection.

Natural_Language: Known or estimated time schedule for growth to ultimate requirements.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_3: Agency must furnish growth schedule to ultimate requirements
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element.

Natural_Language: Estimated ultimate maximum demand and ultimate monthly consumption.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_4: Agency must furnish estimated ultimate maximum demand and monthly consumption
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element.

Natural_Language: A simple schematic diagram or line drawing showing the meter locations, the location of the new utility facilities to be constructed on Federal property by the Federal agency, and any required new connection facilities on either side of the delivery point to be constructed by the utility supplier to provide the new services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_5: Agency must furnish schematic diagram showing meter locations, new facility locations on Federal property, and required connection facilities at delivery point
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element. Technical diagram requirement.

Natural_Language: Accounting and appropriation data to cover the required utility services and any connection charges required to be paid by the agency receiving such utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_6: Agency must furnish accounting and appropriation data for utility services and connection charges
Validation_Notes: Mandatory new service information element. Financial data requirement.

Natural_Language: Data concerning proposed facilities and related charges or costs.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_7: Proposed facilities data requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for facilities data. Both sub-items are required.

Natural_Language: Proposed refundable or nonrefundable connection charge, termination liability, or other facilities charge to be paid by the agency, together with a description of the supplier's proposed facilities and estimated construction costs, and its rationale for the charge (e.g., tariff provisions or policies).
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_7_i_a: Agency must furnish proposed charges (connection, termination, facilities); P_41_301_c_7_i_b: Must include description of supplier proposed facilities and estimated construction costs; P_41_301_c_7_i_c: Must include rationale for charges
Validation_Notes: Multi-element mandatory data requirement. Charges, facilities description, and rationale all required.

Natural_Language: A copy of the acquiring agency's estimate to make its own connection to the supplier's facilities through use of its own resources or by separate contract. When feasible, the acquiring agency must provide its estimates to construct and operate its own utility facilities in lieu of participating in a cost-sharing construction program with the proposed utility supplier.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_c_7_ii_a: Agency must provide estimate for own connection to supplier facilities; P_41_301_c_7_ii_b: When feasible, agency must provide estimates to construct and operate own utility facilities in lieu of cost-sharing
Validation_Notes: Two-part requirement. Own-connection estimate is always mandatory. Self-construction estimate is conditional on feasibility. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: For existing utility service, the agency must furnish GSA the information in paragraph (b) of this section and the additional items in (f)(1) through (f)(5) as applicable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f: Existing service requirements include (b) information plus items (f)(1) through (f)(5)
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for existing service requirements. Cross-references paragraph (b). All items mandatory as applicable.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f_1: Agency must furnish most recent 12-months service invoices
Validation_Notes: Mandatory existing service information element.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f_2: Agency must furnish 12-month tabulation of demands, consumption, charges, and average monthly cost per unit
Validation_Notes: Mandatory existing service information element. Detailed monthly data required.

Natural_Language: An estimate, by month, for the next 12 months, showing the estimated maximum demands, monthly consumption, other pertinent information (e.g., demand side management, load or energy management, peak shaving, on site generation, load shaping), and annual cost of the service.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f_3: Agency must furnish next 12-month estimates of maximum demands, consumption, pertinent information, and annual cost
Validation_Notes: Mandatory existing service information element. Forward-looking projection required.

Natural_Language: Accounting and appropriation data to cover the costs for the continuation of utility services.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f_4: Agency must furnish accounting and appropriation data for continuation of utility services
Validation_Notes: Mandatory existing service information element.

Natural_Language: A statement noting whether the transformer, or other system components, on either side of the delivery point are owned by the Federal agency or the utility supplier, and if the metering is on the primary or secondary side of the transformer.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_301_f_5: Agency must furnish statement of equipment ownership at delivery point and metering location
Validation_Notes: Mandatory existing service information element. Technical ownership and metering details.

Natural_Language: Agencies must review utility service invoices on a monthly basis and all utility accounts, with annual values exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, on an annual basis. Annual reviews of accounts with annual values at or below the simplified acquisition threshold must be conducted when deemed advantageous to the Government. The purpose of the monthly review is to ensure the accuracy of utility service invoices. The purpose of the annual review is to ensure that the utility supplier is furnishing the services to each facility under the utility's most economical, applicable rate and to examine competitive markets for more advantageous service offerings. The annual review must be based upon the facility's usage, conditions and characteristics of service at each individual delivery point for the most recent 12 months. If a more advantageous rate is appropriate, the Federal agency must request the supplier to make such rate change immediately.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_401_a: Agencies must review utility invoices monthly for accuracy; P_41_401_b: Agencies must annually review utility accounts with values exceeding SAT; P_41_401_c: Annual reviews of accounts at or below SAT must be conducted when deemed advantageous; P_41_401_d: Annual review purpose is to ensure most economical rate and examine competitive markets; P_41_401_e: Annual review must be based on most recent 12 months usage at each delivery point; P_41_401_f: If more advantageous rate is appropriate, agency must request rate change immediately
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-element review requirement. Monthly invoice review is mandatory. Annual review mandatory for above-SAT accounts, discretionary for at-or-below-SAT. Annual review methodology and scope specified. Rate change request is conditional on finding a more advantageous rate. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: Rate changes and regulatory intervention provisions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_402: Rate change and regulatory intervention provisions
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for rate changes and intervention.

Natural_Language: When a change is proposed to rates or terms and conditions of service to the Government, the agency must promptly determine whether the proposed change is reasonable, justified, and not discriminatory.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_402_a_1: When rate or terms change is proposed, agency must promptly determine reasonableness; P_41_402_a_2: Agency must determine change is justified; P_41_402_a_3: Agency must determine change is not discriminatory
Validation_Notes: Conditional mandatory requirement. Proposed rate change triggers three-part determination obligation. All three criteria (reasonable, justified, non-discriminatory) must be assessed. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: If a change is proposed to rates or terms and conditions of service that may be of interest to other Federal agencies, and intervention before a regulatory body is considered justified, the matter must be referred to GSA. The agency may request from GSA a delegation of authority for the agency to intervene on behalf of the consumer interests of the Federal executive agencies.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_402_b_a: If multi-agency interest and justified intervention, matter must be referred to GSA; P_41_402_b_b: Agency may request GSA delegation to intervene on behalf of Federal executive agencies
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18

Natural_Language: Pursuant to 52.241-7, Change in Rates or Terms and Conditions of Service for Regulated Services, if a regulatory body approves a rate change, any rate change must be made a part of the contract by unilateral contract modification or otherwise documented in accordance with agency procedures. The approved applicable rate must be effective on the date determined by the regulatory body and resulting rates and charges must be paid promptly to avoid late payment provisions. Copies of the modification containing the approved rate change must be sent to the agency's paying office or office responsible for verifying billed amounts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_402_c_a: Regulatory-approved rate change must be made part of contract by unilateral modification or agency documentation; P_41_402_c_b: Approved rate must be effective on date determined by regulatory body; P_41_402_c_c: Resulting rates and charges must be paid promptly; P_41_402_c_d: Modification copies must be sent to paying office or billing verification office
Validation_Notes: Conditional multi-element requirement triggered by regulatory body approval. Four conjunctive obligations follow approval. Reference to 52.241-7 establishes external dependency. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Natural_Language: If the utility supplier is not regulated and the rates, terms, and conditions of service are subject to negotiation pursuant to the clause at 52.241-8, Change in Rates or Terms and Conditions of Service for Unregulated Services, any rate change must be made a part of the contract by contract modification, with copies sent to the agency's paying office or office responsible for verifying billed amounts.
Atomic_Propositions: P_41_402_d_a: For unregulated suppliers, rate changes must be made part of contract by modification; P_41_402_d_b: Modification copies must be sent to paying office or billing verification office
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement triggered by unregulated supplier status. Two mandatory actions upon rate change. Reference to 52.241-8 establishes external dependency. HIGH-RISK for Rule 15.

Atomic_Propositions: P_41_501: Solicitation provisions and contract clauses for utility services
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for clause requirements.
